q: What end-tidal oxygen is targeted before RSI for obstetric GA?
why: Pre-oxygenate head-up to FeO2 0.9 or more; consider HFNO.

q: After failed intubation in a category 1 caesarean, the mother is oxygenating well via a second-generation SAD and the fetus is compromised. What is reasonable?
o: Wake the mother in all cases
Proceed with surgery on the SAD, with cricoid pressure as appropriate
why: The proceed vs wake decision weighs fetal compromise, maternal condition and airway control; if oxygenating, proceeding on the SAD may be reasonable.

q: What is the delivery target for a category 1 caesarean?
why: Category 1 under 30 minutes; category 2 under 75 minutes.

q: Which intrauterine resuscitation measure is used for fetal distress in labour?
o: Stop oxytocin, left lateral position, fluid bolus, oxygen, and consider terbutaline 250 mcg
why: Stop oxytocin, reposition, give fluid, oxygen and consider a tocolytic.

q: In cord prolapse, how can the presenting part be lifted off the cord while awaiting delivery?
o: Knee–chest or head-down position, manual elevation, or filling the bladder with about 500 ml
why: Keep the cord warm and moist and relieve compression while moving to a category 1 caesarean.

q: Why is a nasopharyngeal airway avoided in pregnancy?
why: Pregnant mucosa is engorged and bleeds easily.

q: When is an opioid usually given during obstetric GA?
o: At induction (e.g. alfentanil or remifentanil), with the neonatal team informed
Only after cord clamping in every case
why: Current UK OAA/DAS practice gives a short-acting opioid at induction to blunt the pressor response and reduce awareness; neonatal effects are mild and transient. Older teaching delayed opioids until after cord clamping. Local practice here: opioid at induction only for pre-eclampsia/PIH.

q: Which questionnaire assesses awareness after GA?
why: The Brice questionnaire is asked at several time points.

q: What size ETT is typically used for obstetric GA?
why: Smaller tubes (6.0–7.0) allow for airway oedema; have a videolaryngoscope available.

q: What is the approximate aspiration incidence in obstetric GA?
why: Around 1 in 500; use antacid prophylaxis and RSI.
